clue.text: Wound soldiers surrounding German's room

indicators.note: to surround something is to sit on both sides of it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
Raum is the German word for room

explanation.surface: A wounded soldier is billeted in a German's room.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a medical term for a physical injury, so it is a synonym of a wound.

clue.text: Dessert - is it a rum concoction?

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up from ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a dessert and wonders if it is just a rum-soaked concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is fair: tiramisu is often laced with rum or Marsala, so the anagram describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, an example of a dessert.

clue.text: Lawyer to sailors caught in a further capsizal

indicators.note: a boat that capsizes turns upside down, which in a down clue flips the word's order
something caught in something else is held inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
yet means further or still more, as in 'yet another'
taken as written
the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A lawyer advises sailors caught up in yet another capsized boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capsizal' applies only to the word for further, not to the whole phrase; the leading A stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a legal representative, the American word for a lawyer.

clue.text: Saw German chap stalking maiden

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German man is stalking a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Stalking means following, so the German's name comes after the maiden. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, and a motto is a short guiding saying, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Usher in very dirty bar

blocks.note: something filthy can be called black with dirt
a rod is a bar of metal or wood

explanation.surface: An usher shows someone into a filthy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub but is just a rod. Black Rod is the official who summons MPs to the House of Lords for the State Opening of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Rod's full title is Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod, a ceremonial officer of the House of Lords.

clue.text: Mistress from Holland may, struggling with it

indicators.note: a struggling thing is thrashing about out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be mixed
added to the mix, joined by 'with'

explanation.surface: A mistress from the Netherlands may be having a hard time of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma, Lady Hamilton was famous as the lover of Admiral Lord Nelson, the best-known mistress in British history.

clue.text: Tell all to turn up ahead of fair

blocks.note: to come is to arrive or turn up
fair play is clean play

explanation.surface: Someone is told to show up early for the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' only places the first piece before the second; 'fair' is not a funfair but an adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for confessing everything, which is what telling all means.

clue.text: Mention about Ecstasy in jacket

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the drug

blocks.note: to refer to something is to mention it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone mentions that there is ecstasy hidden in a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug theme pulls toward the cannabis sense of the answer, but the definition is the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a short, thick double-breasted jacket of the kind worn by sailors.

clue.text: Lovely and vague

blocks.note: first meaning: delightful, wonderful
second meaning: absent-minded, in a world of one's own

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a description of one person, but the two adjectives are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy can mean wonderful, as in a dreamy holiday, or distracted and unfocused, as if half asleep.

clue.text: Go round (run round) gallery

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, and O is round in shape
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A visitor is told to go round, quickly, a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words read like an aside repeating the definition, but they supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis, a synonym of going round.

clue.text: A titled woman crossing border in novel

indicators.note: a figure crossing something straddles it, so one word sits across and around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a dame holds a title, as in Dame Judi Dench
a garden border is a flower bed

explanation.surface: A noblewoman crosses a frontier in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests a frontier but is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is George Eliot's first full-length novel, published in 1859.

clue.text: Film a whole planet exploding

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

blocks.note: letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A movie shows an entire planet blowing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The disaster-movie surface suits the action film the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal Weapon is the 1987 buddy-cop action film starring Mel Gibson and Danny Glover.

clue.text: Touring in the more historic Welsh county

indicators.note: touring means travelling about, so the letters wander into a different order

blocks.note: letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A traveller explores more of an old Welsh county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but its letters belong in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Merioneth, or Merionethshire, was a county of north-west Wales until it was abolished in 1974.

clue.text: Stuff round end of profiterole?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
round means surrounding, so the verb's letters wrap around the single letter

blocks.note: to cram is to stuff full
the final letter of the pastry's name

explanation.surface: A cook asks what goes round the end of a choux bun.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the filling stuffed inside a profiterole surrounds its far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Profiteroles are choux buns piped full of whipped cream, so the clue as a whole describes that filling.

clue.text: One may be used to break rocks in prison, around side by hospital

definitions.text: One may be used to break rocks

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the prison word wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: the slammer is slang for jail
an edge is a side of something
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A tool for breaking rocks in a prison work gang, kept by the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In prison' reads as the convict's setting, but 'in' is the link and prison gives the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledgehammer is a heavy long-handled hammer, the tool of chain-gang convicts breaking stones.

clue.text: Good landlord won't fancy an empty place

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a host is a landlord at an inn
the letters of won't, apostrophe dropped, rearranged

explanation.surface: A decent landlord will not take a liking to a deserted pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb meaning to like but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost town is an abandoned settlement with no inhabitants left, an empty place.

clue.text: Jude Law, a rep in part, bringing one to this US state

indicators.note: only a part of the words is wanted, a run of letters sitting inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters starting in Jude and ending in rep

explanation.surface: The actor Jude Law, playing a repertory role, brings someone to an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' also suggests an actor's role, fitting Jude Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a small state on the US east coast, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: Fireproof material, like finest used by sailor

blocks.note: as means like, in 'as good as gold'
the finest is the best
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor uses the finest fireproof material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used for fire-resistant insulation and protective cloth.

clue.text: Adventuress lends from all, unwisely

indicators.note: acting unwisely means going about things wrongly, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A female adventurer foolishly lends money to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link word but its letters are needed in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Moll Flanders is Daniel Defoe's 1722 heroine, a thief and serial wife who lives by her wits, an adventuress.

clue.text: Sign male's ignored in reference book

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: a male is he, so male's gives he's
a thesaurus is a book of synonyms

explanation.surface: A star sign is missing from the male's reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the bull, is the second sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Iran, an amazing land for children?

indicators.note: amazing comes from maze, so the letters are lost in a tangle and come out reordered

blocks.note: letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Iran is held up as a wonderful country for kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the land is fictional, from children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Narnia is the magical realm in C. S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia, a children's fantasy series.

clue.text: A member, separated

blocks.note: taken as written
a member is a part of a body or a whole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a person in a club, but here it is a limb or component.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept apart are separated from one another, so the adverb matches the participle used predicatively.

clue.text: Clear river containing single rodent

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the river's letters surround the rest

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a single is one
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A river is hiding a lone rat.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of blame, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: To remove all trace of epoch's close to impossible

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: an era is an epoch, so epoch's gives era's
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Wiping out every sign of an age is next to impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to impossible' reads as nearly impossible, but it means the word's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or obliterate, leaving no trace.

clue.text: English poet, Arnold, drunk at public house

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of line, so the name's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: letters to be mixed
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: The poet Matthew Arnold is tipsy in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold looks like the poet's name, but the answer is a different poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Randolph was a 17th-century English poet and dramatist, one of the Sons of Ben Jonson.

clue.text: Empty container into large tank

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the small vessel goes inside the large one

blocks.note: a can is a container
a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: Someone tips a container into a large tank to empty it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' reads as a verb but is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied or containing nothing, a synonym of empty.

clue.text: Sluggish beast, before noon, followed by worker

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer
N is the abbreviation for noon
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A slow animal, seen before midday, is trailed by a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water barely moves, and figuratively it describes slow, inactive trade or growth.

clue.text: Break in bay

blocks.note: first meaning: a pause, as between school lessons
second meaning: an alcove set back in a wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Break in' looks like a burglary, but the two words are separate senses joined by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both an interval in proceedings and a hollow set into a wall, like a bay or niche.
